button.label: Check DNS
button.supertip: Select a column of IP addresses or hostnames, then click. For each one NetTools does a forward lookup, a reverse (PTR) lookup, checks they agree, and pings it. Results go on the 'DNS Check' sheet as a table (overwritten on each run) - your data is not changed. Press Esc to stop.

button.label: DNS Only
button.supertip: Forward and reverse lookup only - no ping. Results go on the 'DNS Lookup' sheet.

button.label: Ping Only
button.supertip: Ping each host 4 times and report status, replies, average latency and TTL on the 'Ping' sheet.

button.label: Port Check
button.supertip: Checks whether TCP ports (e.g. 22, 443, 3389) are open on each selected host. Open = accepted, Closed = refused, Filtered = no answer. Results go on the 'Port Check' sheet.

button.label: Traceroute
button.supertip: Hop-by-hop path to each selected host (3 probes per hop, like tracert). Each trace goes on its own 'Trace host' sheet. Select an empty cell to type a host instead.

button.label: Subnet Scan
button.supertip: Pings every address in a subnet (10.1.4.0/24 or 10.1.4.0 255.255.255.0) - hundreds at once - and shows MAC address + vendor (local subnets), reverse DNS and, optionally, open TCP ports. Each subnet goes on its own 'Scan' sheet, overwritten when you scan it again. Select an empty cell to type the subnet.

button.label: Subnet Calc
button.supertip: For each selected subnet (10.1.4.0/22 or 10.1.4.7 255.255.252.0): network, mask, wildcard, first/last usable, broadcast and host count, on the 'Subnets' sheet. Select an empty cell to type subnets instead.

button.label: MAC Format
button.supertip: Reformats the selected MAC addresses as xxxx.xxxx.xxxx or XX:XX:XX:XX:XX:XX (you choose) and looks up the vendor. Results go on the 'MAC Addresses' sheet.

button.label: SSH Logs
button.supertip: SSH into the selected Cisco IOS / IOS-XE / 9800 or AireOS devices with your username and password, run commands such as show logging, and put each device's output on its own sheet (also saved under Documents\NetTools\SSH Logs). The password is never saved.
